Football fans need to accept one thing despite Man City charges verdict

Tom Procter
Wed 7 October 2026 17:00, UK
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:11
Instaread

People continue to debate what Manchester City’s punishment should be, after the club were found guilty by an independent Commission of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League’s financial regulations between the 2009/10 and 2017/18 seasons.

Manchester City have appealed, and the hearing lasts for five days. The deadline for the appeal conclusion is December 24, and the deadline for the appeal verdict is on January 24 (via SI).

City were ruled to have organised ‘sham contracts’ to artificially inflate the club’s revenues and reduce its costs. The club will supposedly try to argue that the money came from the Abu Dhabi government and not the owners. Other Premier League clubs want severe punishment for City, given how long this was happening.

The appeal is now ongoing, but football fans far and wide are sticking the boot in following the damning verdict by the independent Commission.

Many have argued that City’s successes between 09/10 and 17/18 are now tainted. But even if City’s appeal fails, there is an argument to say that the personal achievements of the players are not.

Man City have confirmed that they are appealing the recent guilty verdict in relation to breaching Premier League regulations. How do you expect the appeal to go?

Man City past players’ achievements wouldn’t be tainted despite guilty verdict

Naturally, a lot of people have gone in on City following the bombshell that arrived just under a couple of weeks ago.

What has happened is unprecedented, and the book should be thrown at City if the appeal fails.

But the wrongdoings of the hierarchy should be separated from the players, who have merely done their jobs as footballers.

Perhaps the way in which many were brought to the Etihad Stadium were wrong. We await to see the outcome of the appeal on that. But many of the players did special things in the City shirt and they should still be admired and revered for that.

Players don’t sit in accountancy meetings or take part in structuring corporate sponsorships. They’re employees whose sole job is to carry out tactical instructions, maintain elite physical fitness, and win football matches.

Ultimately, no amount of financial structuring can teach a player how to dance through a sea of defenders, execute a perfect tactical press, score a last-minute winner or even maintain the mental resilience required to win continuous league titles.

The likes of Sergio Aguero, David Silva, Yaya Toure, Kevin De Bruyne and Rodri developed into generational talents. Their growth and world-class performances were a testament to their personal dedication and coaching, not corporate balance sheets.

Framing achievements like De Bruyne twice winning Player of the Season, or Aguero winning a Golden Boot, as ‘tainted’ is just lazy narrative that ignores the historic sporting standards this specific group of players set for English football.

When the dust finally settles on this legal saga, the legacy of past City players shouldn’t be defined by financial statements or the cynical narratives of rival fans. If City are punished heavily, then it’s important that rival fans focus on the board and not try to diminish the success of the players themselves.
